I’ll preserve and audit the failed capture, then check whether the source change affected the measurement. I’m using the SASE memory, repository, and monitor skills to recover valid coverage and continue the analysis.


Both TUIs restarted at about 11:02 EDT onto the same newer revision, with the measurement flags intact. The prior segments contain only 30 minutes of usable Athena coverage and one Apollo heartbeat. I’ll retain those segments and update the collector to preserve future revision changes separately, without pooling their measurements.


The revision change contains only a monitor test; the TUI and GC code is unchanged. Four-hour coverage still needs one uninterrupted TUI instance per host. Please leave both running and use normal navigation, including j/k. I’ll also measure the suspected allocation producers so the next capture yields more than coverage data.


The census points to two concrete sources of cyclic garbage: rendering objects and copied Agent graphs. I found two Textual operations that can cache a Strip inside itself. I’m testing those cycles and measuring graph copies, fleet projection, link snapshots, and the large event-model populations separately.


The experiments confirm both kinds of cycles. Rendering 1,000 Strips with self-caching operations leaves roughly 1.4 MB awaiting GC; copying 100 linked Agent rows leaves roughly 0.8 MB. Unchanged artifact-link snapshots reuse the cache with very little allocation. I also found that the workspace’s dependency versions differ from the installed TUI’s, so I’m rerunning the producer measurements with the installed dependencies.


In Athena’s interrupted 30-minute segment, ordinary idle collections still had a 2.18-second p95 after excluding census-associated collectors. GC consumed 6.98% of the recorded interval, and swap peaked near 253 MiB. These are useful failure measurements, but neither host has the required four-hour window yet.


The recovered collector passed 13 coverage checks and is recording both current instances. If they stay running, the four-hour RSS windows should finish around 15:25 EDT. Apollo still needs current-instance j/k samples for the navigation comparison. I’m preserving the producer results and handing the remaining capture to SASE monitor.
